As part of the approval to develop sites under Conditional Use Permit No. 17-10, the Developer is conditioned to dedicate certain streets deemed necessary for public use to current City standards, vacate certain offers of dedication, and to provide covenants and easements for certain streets deemed necessary for future private access that supersede the existing offers of dedication. CC 6. Approve the Reimbursement Agreement for the Construction of Master Planned Drainage Facilities with K. Hovnanian Communities, Inc.
K.
Hovnanian Communities, Inc., previously paid the entire drainage impact fees for Tract No. 54401, so no impact fee credit will be issued. The cost of the MPDF will be reimbursed through annual reimbursements to be paid out of drainage impact fees collected. City policy states a maximum of twenty percent of the drainage impact fees collected each year may be used to pay for reimbursements. If more than one reimbursement agreement is in effect during the year, each agreement shall receive a percentage of the twenty percent of the total drainage impact fees collected for that year.

Becker and Son, Inc., of Santa Clarita, California, in the amount of $1,913,726.91, plus a 10% contingency, to install bulb-outs, curb ramps, sidewalk, landscaping and irrigation, storm drainage improvements, pavement rehabilitation, utility improvements, signing, striping and markings and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to sign all documents. This contract is awarded to the lowest responsible bidder per California Public Code Section 22038 (b).
The project includes intersection improvements to install bulb-outs, curb ramps, sidewalk, landscaping and irrigation, storm drainage improvements, pavement rehabilitation, utility improvements, signing, striping and markings. Work will be performed in compliance with the Cityâ€™s 2014 ADA Transition Plan.

Becker and Son, Inc., of Santa Clarita, California, in the amount of $2,041,130.30, plus a 10% contingency, for roadway reconstruction and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to sign all documents. This contract is awarded to the lowest responsible bidder per California Public Code Section 22038 (b).
The project involves reconstruction of the street section, lowering the crown of the road and installation of landscaped medians, restriping, and curb ramp modifications. Work will be performed in compliance with the Cityâ€™s 2014 ADA Transition Plan, which will include reconstruction of four (4) curb ramps, twelve (12) commercial driveways, eight (8) residential driveways, repair of 1,764 square feet of sidewalk, and the addition of 4,469 square feet of residential sidewalk.

CC 9. Approve the appropriation of $39,277.00 in grant funds from the California Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) to Expense Account No. 330-4755-775
The City was awarded $39,277.00 in grant funds from the California Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) for Fiscal Year 2016-17 to fund recycling education and awareness, beverage container recycling programs, and litter removal. Expenditure of these grant funds must be incurred no later than June 29, 2020. Additionally, funds are allotted towards administrative costs to monitor, report, and coordinate grant activities. These funds will be used to promote recycling in various areas.

PH 1. Approve the Substantial Amendment for the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Consolidated Annual Action Plan for the 2016-2017 and 2017-2018 Program Year from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
Recommendation:
Approve the Substantial Amendment for the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Annual Action Plan for the 2016-2017 and 2017-2018 Program Year to be submitted to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). The amendment will reallocate unexpended PY 2016-2017 funds from the Homelessness Services activity and delete/reallocate funds from the PY 2017-2018 Homelessness Services activity. Said funds would be used to further the objectives of the four existing Master Plan Community Developments along with the four additionally proposed Master Plan Community Developments.
The new activities meet Consolidated Plan â€“ Strategic Plan Goals. These activities will cover costs associated with the preparation of the tentative tract and final tract maps necessary to develop land as affordable housing for very low-, low-, median-, and moderate income households.

PH 2. Appeal of the Planning Commissionâ€™s Denial of Conditional Use Permit No. 17-11 for a Proposed Development Located at 1966 West Avenue L
Recommendation:
Defer the decision for a proposed conditional use permit application to the Planning Commission for review and reconsideration; the proposed application for development would include a gas canopy island, car wash facility, oil and lube facility, mini-mart with a Type 20 (off-sale beer and wine) Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) license, and waiver from the required distance requirements.
In matters where appeals are made to the City Council, the Lancaster Municipal Code Section 2.44.060.C provides that the City Council can â€œrefer the matter back to the commission, board, or city official for further proceeding with or without instruction.â€ Staff recommends that City Council refer the proposed project back before Planning Commission for further consideration.

NB 1. Introduction of Ordinance reauthorizing Ordinance to preserve City of Lancasterâ€™s right to continue collecting PEG fees under state law
Recommendation:
Introduce Ordinance No. 1038, reauthorizing Ordinance No. 897, permitting the City of Lancaster (the â€œCityâ€) to continue the status quo in receiving State Franchise fees and PEG fees from its cable/video TV operators.
Section 5870(n) of the Public Utilities Code requires that Ordinance No. 897 be reauthorized upon the expiration of the state franchise. California granted Time Warner Cable Pacific West LLC, dba Charter Communications (â€œCharterâ€), a state video franchise, which expired on January 2, 2018. As such, the City must approve Ordinance No. 1038, reauthorizing Ordinance No. 897; in order to continue the status quo in receiving State Franchise fees and PEG fees from all state-franchised video service providers.
